name: RobustGenBench
description: RobustGenBench is a standardized benchmark for robust generalization of image classifiers: how accuracy holds up across perturbation types a model was not trained against. It packages six classification datasets (Caltech-101, FGVC-Aircraft, Flowers-102, Oxford-IIIT Pet, Stanford Cars, UC Merced Land Use) with fixed train/validation/test splits, images resized to 224x224, and test sets capped at 1,000 images (420 for UC Merced; 5,420 test images in total). Each dataset config holds the clean splits, a common-corruption split (11 corruption types at severity 3, assigned deterministically, one per image) and a random uniform-noise control (l-infinity, 30/255). Each <dataset>-<surrogate> config holds adversarial test images crafted with AutoAttack on an open-weight vision-language surrogate (CLIP ViT-B/16, CLIP ViT-H/14, MetaCLIP ViT-H/14, SigLIP2 SO400M, SigLIP2 base) at l1 in {75, 300}, l2 in {2, 8} and l-infinity in {4, 8, 30}/255. Because these perturbations transfer, any model, including API-only vision-enabled LLMs, can be evaluated by inference alone. Companion code: https://github.com/legolasflagstaff/robustgenbench
citation: RobustGenBench: Benchmarking Robust Generalization to Unforeseen Adversarial and Common Perturbations in Vision Models and Vision-Enabled LLMs
rai:dataCollection: No new images were collected. The clean images come from six public datasets, organized into fixed train/validation/test splits, resized to 224x224 and stored as lossless PNG. Test sets were reduced to at most 1,000 images by uniform sampling that preserves all classes.
rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is bounded by the six source datasets (objects, aircraft, flowers, pets, cars, aerial land use). Robustness measured here should not be read as robustness on open-world imagery or other domains.

Adversarial images are crafted white-box on five fixed open-weight surrogates, all attention-based, and act as transfer (black-box) attacks for any other model. For a model with gradient access, they are not a substitute for white-box or adaptive evaluation, which the companion code runs on the clean test splits (as done for the fine-tuned vision models in the paper). Transfer is also weaker to architectures unlike the surrogates (e.g., convolutional networks).

Surrogates only attack images they classify correctly; images the surrogate misclassifies are stored unmodified (is_modified = false). SigLIP2 SO400M adversarial splits exist only for the coarse-grained datasets (Caltech-101, Flowers-102, UC Merced), and SigLIP2 base only at l-infinity 30/255.

Common corruptions are provided at a single severity (3); adversarial perturbations are provided at several budgets per norm (l1 75/300, l2 2/8, l-infinity 4/8/30 /255). Budgets are not matched across norms, so cross-norm comparisons depend on the chosen intensities.
Images are 224x224; results may not transfer to models evaluated at other resolutions without resizing.
rai:dataBiases: The source datasets reflect the content and collection choices of their original authors (e.g., car models from a narrow period, pet breeds common in the UK, web-scraped Caltech-101 imagery with known class imbalance). These selection biases carry over to every robustness score.

Transfer-attack strength varies by dataset and class with the surrogate's own zero-shot accuracy (e.g., weak SigLIP2 accuracy on fine-grained datasets), so per-class and per-dataset robustness signals are uneven.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains no annotated personal or sensitive attributes. Some source images may incidentally show people, faces or license plates (e.g., Caltech-101, Stanford Cars, Oxford-IIIT Pet). No anonymization beyond the source datasets was applied.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended: held-out evaluation of how image classifiers (fine-tuned vision models, zero-shot models, API-only vision-enabled LLMs) generalize across common and l1/l2/l-infinity perturbations, using the protocol and metrics (Sum, Borda, MAC) of the associated paper.
Intended: crafting new perturbations on the clean test splits for white-box evaluation, and robust fine-tuning on the clean train/validation splits.
Not validated for: training general-purpose recognition models, fairness or demographic auditing, or robustness claims outside the six domains and the included budgets.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to make robustness comparisons reproducible and cheap: the pre-computed attacks remove the need for high-memory GPUs, so models can be tested before deployment. The released adversarial images could also be used to probe deployed systems; they are standard l-p transfer attacks on public datasets, the release is limited to non-commercial research use (CC BY-NC 4.0, plus the source datasets' terms), and the domains covered are narrow.
rai:hasSyntheticDataDescription: Common-corruption, random-noise and adversarial splits are procedurally perturbed versions of the natural source images (imgaug corruptions, uniform l-infinity noise, AutoAttack). No images were produced by generative models.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: (1) Source datasets were downloaded from their official pages and organized into fixed train/validation/test splits; test sets were capped at 1,000 images with class-preserving uniform sampling. (2) Original images were resized from their native resolutions to a common 224x224 and stored as lossless PNG. (3) Common corruptions: 11 ImageNet-C-style corruption types (imgaug) at severity 3, assigned to test images in contiguous blocks (type floor(i/s) mod 11, s = floor(N/11)), one corruption per image. (4) Random control: uniform noise in the l-infinity ball of radius 30/255, clipped to [0, 1]. (5) Adversarial: white-box AutoAttack (standard version) against zero-shot classifiers built from each surrogate ('a photo of a {class}' text prompts), released for use as transfer attacks on other models, at l1 75/300, l2 2/8, l-infinity 4/8/30 (/255), in the 224x224 input space (SigLIP2 SO400M upsamples to 384 inside its forward pass). (6) All splits are stored as Parquet. Version 2.1 restores the common split of the original processed archives (tag v1.0-archives). Code: https://github.com/legolasflagstaff/robustgenbench
